When authoritative reconciliation is unavailable after W2 receives conflict/already-exists, W2 cannot safely reinterpret the conflict as idempotent success because the canonical payload is unknown to that actor; it must preserve an unresolved conflict state and emit no create or overwrite.

Both actor states are durably checkpointable without a new mutation by retaining effect identity, intended payload hash, prior submission/result and a reconciliation-pending flag, allowing a later invocation to reconcile before any further effectful action.

The outage therefore preserves safety but not liveness: exactly one canonical effect remains in this fixture, while neither actor is permitted to claim a fully reconciled terminal outcome during the lookup outage.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, fail-closed checkpointing across a reconciliation outage prevents duplicate/conflicting mutations after both acknowledgement loss and loser conflict, but it does not establish liveness or transport availability. A recurring-Chat claim protocol can remain safe across a rate-limit interruption only if it persists enough local intent/submission state to defer all mutation retries until a later authoritative lookup; prolonged lookup unavailability remains an unresolved child rather than a success state.
